item.title: ATS Resume Improver: Free AI-Powered Resume Optimizer
item.category: "Career Tools" , "Open Source Projects" , "Artificial Intelligence" , "Privacy Technology" , "Developer Tools" , "Job Hunting" , "Productivity"
item.description: ATS Resume Improver is a free, open-source, client-side resume optimizer supporting OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and local Ollama models. Parse, score, keyword-match, optimize, and export your resume — all without your data leaving the browser.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Free, open-source, and self-hostable. Your resume never touches a server unless you use an AI provider — and even then, it goes directly to the AI provider, not to us.</strong></p> <h2 id="what-is-ats-resume-improver"> <a href="#what-is-ats-resume-improver" title="What Is ATS Resume Improver?">What Is ATS Resume Improver?</a> <a href="#what-is-ats-resume-improver" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What Is ATS Resume Improver?">#</a> </h2> <p><strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="ATS Resume Improver"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/"> <a href="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >ATS Resume Improver</a> </span> </strong> is an open-source, browser-based resume optimizer that analyzes your resume against a job description and helps you close the gap between what you have and what applicant tracking systems actually score. Built with React 19, Vite, and TypeScript, the entire <strong>parsing and scoring pipeline runs inside your browser</strong> with no backend server.</p> <p>The source code is at <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver"> <a href="https://github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver</a> </span> </strong>. You can use the hosted version, deploy your own to Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare/GitHub Pages in one click, or spin it up locally with Docker.</p> <h3 id="the-privacy-problem-it-solves"> <a href="#the-privacy-problem-it-solves" title="The Privacy Problem It Solves">The Privacy Problem It Solves</a> <a href="#the-privacy-problem-it-solves" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Privacy Problem It Solves">#</a> </h3> <p>Most resume optimization services upload your resume to their servers, run proprietary scoring, and retain your data. ATS Resume Improver takes the opposite approach.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Mode</th> <th>What leaves your device</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>No AI key</strong></td> <td>Nothing — 100% local, runs in your browser</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>OpenAI / Anthropic</strong></td> <td>Resume text + job description go directly to the AI provider API using your key — no intermediate server</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Ollama (local)</strong></td> <td>Nothing — model runs on your own machine</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>API keys are stored in memory only</strong> — they disappear when you close the tab. No analytics, no tracking, no cookies.</p> <hr> <h2 id="core-features"> <a href="#core-features" title="Core Features">Core Features</a> <a href="#core-features" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Core Features">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="what-works-without-any-ai-key"> <a href="#what-works-without-any-ai-key" title="What Works Without Any AI Key">What Works Without Any AI Key</a> <a href="#what-works-without-any-ai-key" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What Works Without Any AI Key">#</a> </h3> <p>You don’t need an API key to get real value. The no-key mode includes:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Resume upload</strong> — PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown</li> <li><strong>ATS text extraction</strong> — shows exactly what an ATS parses from your file, including what gets lost in formatting</li> <li><strong>Resume type detection</strong> — automatically identifies which of 7 profiles your resume matches and adapts the section ordering accordingly</li> <li><strong>Section detection and formatting warnings</strong> — flags missing sections and parser-hostile formats</li> <li><strong>ATS score (0–100)</strong> with a 5-dimension breakdown</li> <li><strong>Keyword gap analysis</strong> — rule-based string matching against the job description</li> <li><strong>Deterministic ATS optimization</strong> — local rule-based restructuring</li> <li><strong>Before/after diff viewer</strong> — see exactly what changed</li> <li><strong>Professional PDF, DOCX, TXT, and Markdown export</strong></li> </ul> <h3 id="what-ai-unlocks"> <a href="#what-ai-unlocks" title="What AI Unlocks">What AI Unlocks</a> <a href="#what-ai-unlocks" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What AI Unlocks">#</a> </h3> <p>Connect OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, or local Ollama and the tool upgrades to:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Semantic keyword analysis</strong> — understands context, not just string matches. Shows match strength (Strong/Moderate/Partial), match location (“found in Skills and 3 job roles”), per-keyword importance (Critical/High/Medium/Low), and a 2-3 sentence AI narrative summary</li> <li><strong>AI resume optimization</strong> — full AI rewrite with ATS best-practice prompts</li> <li><strong>AI-enhanced exports</strong> — PDF/DOCX formatted by the AI before download</li> <li><strong>Cover letter generation</strong> — with humanization rules that eliminate AI giveaways (see below)</li> <li><strong>Interview question predictor</strong> — based on the job description</li> <li><strong>Salary range estimator</strong></li> </ul> <hr> <h2 id="resume-type-detection"> <a href="#resume-type-detection" title="Resume Type Detection">Resume Type Detection</a> <a href="#resume-type-detection" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resume Type Detection">#</a> </h2> <p>The app automatically classifies your resume into one of 7 profiles and adjusts section order to match recruiter and ATS expectations for that career stage:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Profile</th> <th>Best For</th> <th>Section Priority</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>🏢 <strong>Experienced Professional</strong></td> <td>5+ years, linear career</td> <td>Experience → Skills → Education</td> </tr> <tr> <td>🌱 <strong>Mid-Level</strong></td> <td>2–5 years</td> <td>Experience → Skills → Education</td> </tr> <tr> <td>🎓 <strong>Entry-Level</strong></td> <td>0–2 years</td> <td>Skills → Education → Projects → Experience</td> </tr> <tr> <td>🎒 <strong>Student / New Grad</strong></td> <td>Still enrolled</td> <td>Education → Projects → Skills → Experience</td> </tr> <tr> <td>🔬 <strong>Academic / Researcher</strong></td> <td>PhD, publications</td> <td>Education → Research → Publications → Experience</td> </tr> <tr> <td>📜 <strong>Certification-Heavy</strong></td> <td>Certs outweigh degree</td> <td>Certifications → Skills → Experience → Education</td> </tr> <tr> <td>🔄 <strong>Career Changer</strong></td> <td>Gap or pivot detected</td> <td>Summary → Transferable Skills → Education → Experience</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><em>Section ordering applies consistently across optimization, PDF, DOCX, TXT, and Markdown exports — not just on screen.</em></p> <hr> <h2 id="ai-semantic-keyword-analysis"> <a href="#ai-semantic-keyword-analysis" title="AI Semantic Keyword Analysis">AI Semantic Keyword Analysis</a> <a href="#ai-semantic-keyword-analysis" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="AI Semantic Keyword Analysis">#</a> </h2> <p>This is where the tool separates from basic keyword counters. When an AI provider is configured, the keyword gap analysis upgrades from simple string matching to semantic reasoning:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Dimension</th> <th>Without AI</th> <th>With AI</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Matching method</strong></td> <td>Exact string match only</td> <td>Semantic understanding of context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Match strength</strong></td> <td>—</td> <td>Strong / Moderate / Partial ratings</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Match context</strong></td> <td>—</td> <td>“found in Skills and 3 job roles”</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Gap importance</strong></td> <td>All gaps treated equal</td> <td>Critical / High / Medium / Low</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Suggestions</strong></td> <td>Generic tips</td> <td>Per-keyword actionable suggestions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Coverage %</strong></td> <td>String-count based</td> <td>Semantically weighted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Summary</strong></td> <td>—</td> <td>2–3 sentence AI narrative</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><em>Local rule-based analysis still runs instantly. AI results enrich it asynchronously while you review.</em></p> <hr> <h2 id="supported-ai-providers"> <a href="#supported-ai-providers" title="Supported AI Providers">Supported AI Providers</a> <a href="#supported-ai-providers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Supported AI Providers">#</a> </h2> <p>All AI calls include ATS best-practice prompts derived from Harvard OCS and Columbia CCE guidelines.</p> <h3 id="openai"> <a href="#openai" title="OpenAI">OpenAI</a> <a href="#openai" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="OpenAI">#</a> </h3> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th>Best For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>GPT-4.1 mini</strong> (default)</td> <td>Smartest fast and affordable — recommended</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPT-4o mini</td> <td>Fast and affordable classic</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPT-4.1</td> <td>Latest GPT-4.1 — sharp instruction following</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPT-4o</td> <td>High quality flagship</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPT-4 Turbo</td> <td>Large context window</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPT-3.5 Turbo</td> <td>Fastest and cheapest</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Estimated cost</strong>: ~$0.002–0.05 per resume analysis.</p> <h3 id="anthropic-claude"> <a href="#anthropic-claude" title="Anthropic Claude">Anthropic Claude</a> <a href="#anthropic-claude" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Anthropic Claude">#</a> </h3> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th>Best For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Claude Sonnet 4.5</strong> (default)</td> <td>Fast and intelligent — recommended</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Claude Opus 4.5</td> <td>Most capable — best for complex tasks</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Claude Haiku 4.5</td> <td>Fastest and cheapest</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Claude 3.5 Sonnet</td> <td>Reliable and well-tested</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Claude 3.5 Haiku</td> <td>Fast and affordable v3.5</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h3 id="ollama-local--self-hosted"> <a href="#ollama-local--self-hosted" title="Ollama (Local / Self-Hosted)">Ollama (Local / Self-Hosted)</a> <a href="#ollama-local--self-hosted" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Ollama (Local / Self-Hosted)">#</a> </h3> <p>No API key required. Run the model on your own hardware. Set <code>OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*</code> to allow browser access.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th>Notes</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Llama 3.3</strong> (default)</td> <td>Latest Meta Llama — recommended</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Llama 3.2</td> <td>Meta Llama 3.2</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mistral 7B</td> <td>Fast and capable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mixtral 8x7B</td> <td>Mixture of experts</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen 2.5</td> <td>Alibaba Qwen 2.5</td> </tr> <tr> <td>DeepSeek R1</td> <td>Strong reasoning model</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Phi-4</td> <td>Microsoft Phi-4</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Gemma 3</td> <td>Google Gemma 3</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Running Ollama locally takes the entire tool fully offline. Nothing leaves your machine at any point.</p> <hr> <h2 id="cover-letter-humanization"> <a href="#cover-letter-humanization" title="Cover Letter Humanization">Cover Letter Humanization</a> <a href="#cover-letter-humanization" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Cover Letter Humanization">#</a> </h2> <p>The cover letter generator applies a deliberate writing style guide to eliminate the telltale signs of AI-generated text. Inspired by <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Sabrina Ramonov’s humanization framework"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.sabrina.dev/p/best-ai-prompt-to-humanize-ai-writing"> <a href="https://www.sabrina.dev/p/best-ai-prompt-to-humanize-ai-writing" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Sabrina Ramonov’s humanization framework</a> </span> , every generated letter enforces these rules:</p> <ul> <li><strong>No em dashes</strong> — the single strongest AI giveaway, removed entirely</li> <li><strong>50+ banned words and phrases</strong>: leverage, utilize, dive deep, delve, embark, game-changer, groundbreaking, cutting-edge, pivotal, tapestry, harness, moreover, in conclusion, it’s worth noting, ever-evolving, landscape, testament, not only…but also, and more</li> <li><strong>No markdown in the letter body</strong> — no bold asterisks, hashtags, or semicolons</li> <li><strong>Active voice by default</strong> — passive only when the actor genuinely doesn’t matter</li> <li><strong>Contractions required</strong>: “I’ve”, “I’m”, “it’s” — never “I have”, “I am”, “it is”</li> <li><strong>Varied sentence length</strong> — short punchy sentences mixed with longer ones</li> <li><strong>No filler openers</strong> — “It’s important to note that X” → just say X</li> <li><strong>Concrete job-posting detail in paragraph 1</strong> — proves the letter wasn’t templated</li> </ul> <p><em>The result reads like a human wrote it — because the rules force the model to write like one.</em></p> <hr> <h2 id="export-quality"> <a href="#export-quality" title="Export Quality">Export Quality</a> <a href="#export-quality" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Export Quality">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Format</th> <th>What You Get</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>PDF</strong></td> <td>Professional typography, section rules, bullet points, contact header</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>DOCX</strong></td> <td>Properly structured Word document (Packer.toBlob — browser-compatible)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TXT</strong></td> <td>Clean plain-text with consistent spacing (ATS-safe)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Markdown</strong></td> <td>Structured <code>.md</code> with headings and bullet lists</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>With an AI provider configured, exports are AI-formatted before download (marked with an ✨ AI-Enhanced badge).</p> <hr> <h2 id="self-hosting-options"> <a href="#self-hosting-options" title="Self-Hosting Options">Self-Hosting Options</a> <a href="#self-hosting-options" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Self-Hosting Options">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="hosted-version-zero-setup"> <a href="#hosted-version-zero-setup" title="Hosted Version (Zero Setup)">Hosted Version (Zero Setup)</a> <a href="#hosted-version-zero-setup" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Hosted Version (Zero Setup)">#</a> </h3> <p>Use the live app at <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="atsresumeimprover.netlify.app"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/"> <a href="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >atsresumeimprover.netlify.app</a> </span> </strong> — no account, no signup, no credit card.</p> <h3 id="one-click-cloud-deploy"> <a href="#one-click-cloud-deploy" title="One-Click Cloud Deploy">One-Click Cloud Deploy</a> <a href="#one-click-cloud-deploy" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="One-Click Cloud Deploy">#</a> </h3> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Platform</th> <th>Link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Vercel</strong></td> <td>One-click deploy from the repo</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Cloudflare Pages</strong></td> <td>One-click deploy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Netlify</strong></td> <td>One-click deploy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>GitHub Pages</strong></td> <td>Fork → Settings → Pages → GitHub Actions → auto-deploys</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h3 id="local-development"> <a href="#local-development" title="Local Development">Local Development</a> <a href="#local-development" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Local Development">#</a> </h3> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>git clone https://github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cd ats-resume-improver </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make install </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make dev <span style="color:#75715e"># http://localhost:5173</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="docker-recommended-for-reproducible-environments"> <a href="#docker-recommended-for-reproducible-environments" title="Docker (Recommended for Reproducible Environments)">Docker (Recommended for Reproducible Environments)</a> <a href="#docker-recommended-for-reproducible-environments" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Docker (Recommended for Reproducible Environments)">#</a> </h3> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Development — hot-reload on http://localhost:5173</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make docker-dev </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Production — nginx on http://localhost:8080</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make docker-prod </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Dev + Ollama together (full local AI stack)</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make docker-dev-with-ollama </span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="ollama-full-offline-stack"> <a href="#ollama-full-offline-stack" title="Ollama Full-Offline Stack">Ollama Full-Offline Stack</a> <a href="#ollama-full-offline-stack" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Ollama Full-Offline Stack">#</a> </h3> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Start Ollama container (persists models across restarts)</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make ollama </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Pull a model</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make ollama-pull MODEL<span style="color:#f92672">=</span>llama3.2 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># Start dev app + Ollama side-by-side</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>make docker-dev-with-ollama </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Then open the app, go to the API key panel, select <strong>Ollama (Local)</strong>, set URL to <code>http://localhost:11434</code>, and pick a model. Zero data leaves your machine.</p> <hr> <h2 id="tech-stack"> <a href="#tech-stack" title="Tech Stack">Tech Stack</a> <a href="#tech-stack" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Tech Stack">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Layer</th> <th>Technology</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Framework</strong></td> <td>React 19 + TypeScript</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Build</strong></td> <td>Vite 8</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Styling</strong></td> <td>Tailwind CSS v4</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Icons</strong></td> <td>Lucide React</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>PDF Parse</strong></td> <td>pdfjs-dist</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>DOCX Parse</strong></td> <td>mammoth</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>PDF Export</strong></td> <td>jsPDF</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>DOCX Export</strong></td> <td>docx (Packer.toBlob)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>AI</strong></td> <td>OpenAI · Anthropic Claude · Ollama</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Container</strong></td> <td>Docker + nginx (multi-stage) + Ollama service</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The entire scoring and parsing pipeline (<code>atsAnalyzer.ts</code>, <code>keywordMatcher.ts</code>, <code>resumeTypeDetector.ts</code>) runs in the browser. All AI integrations in <code>aiProvider.ts</code> call the provider APIs directly from the client — there is no proxy server.</p> <hr> <h2 id="practical-usage-guide"> <a href="#practical-usage-guide" title="Practical Usage Guide">Practical Usage Guide</a> <a href="#practical-usage-guide" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Practical Usage Guide">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="step-1-upload-your-resume"> <a href="#step-1-upload-your-resume" title="Step 1: Upload Your Resume">Step 1: Upload Your Resume</a> <a href="#step-1-upload-your-resume" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 1: Upload Your Resume">#</a> </h3> <p>Upload a PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown file. Switch to the <strong>“What the ATS Sees”</strong> tab to check whether the parser extracted your content cleanly. If sections are missing or mangled in this view, recruiters’ ATS software will have the same problem.</p> <h3 id="step-2-paste-the-job-description"> <a href="#step-2-paste-the-job-description" title="Step 2: Paste the Job Description">Step 2: Paste the Job Description</a> <a href="#step-2-paste-the-job-description" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 2: Paste the Job Description">#</a> </h3> <p>Paste the full job posting into the Job Description panel. More complete job postings produce better keyword analysis — don’t trim the requirements section.</p> <h3 id="step-3-review-your-ats-score"> <a href="#step-3-review-your-ats-score" title="Step 3: Review Your ATS Score">Step 3: Review Your ATS Score</a> <a href="#step-3-review-your-ats-score" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 3: Review Your ATS Score">#</a> </h3> <p>The score panel shows an overall 0–100 score and a 5-dimension breakdown. The dimension breakdown tells you where to focus: format issues lower one dimension, missing keywords lower another, weak work history statements lower a third.</p> <h3 id="step-4-audit-the-keyword-gap"> <a href="#step-4-audit-the-keyword-gap" title="Step 4: Audit the Keyword Gap">Step 4: Audit the Keyword Gap</a> <a href="#step-4-audit-the-keyword-gap" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 4: Audit the Keyword Gap">#</a> </h3> <p>The Keyword Analysis view shows which keywords from the job description appear in your resume and which don’t. With AI enabled, you get semantic matching and importance ratings — a “Critical” gap in a core technical skill is worth more attention than a “Low” gap in a soft-skill buzzword.</p> <h3 id="step-5-optimize"> <a href="#step-5-optimize" title="Step 5: Optimize">Step 5: Optimize</a> <a href="#step-5-optimize" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 5: Optimize">#</a> </h3> <ul> <li><strong>Deterministic mode</strong>: applies rule-based restructuring — safe, fast, no API cost</li> <li><strong>AI mode</strong>: full LLM rewrite using ATS best-practice prompts</li> </ul> <p>Review the <strong>before/after diff</strong> to understand every change before accepting it.</p> <h3 id="step-6-export"> <a href="#step-6-export" title="Step 6: Export">Step 6: Export</a> <a href="#step-6-export" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Step 6: Export">#</a> </h3> <p>Export to PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown. With AI enabled, the export is AI-formatted for professional presentation. The PDF template uses proper typography and recruiter-standard layout.</p> <hr> <h2 id="resume-tips-integration"> <a href="#resume-tips-integration" title="Resume Tips Integration">Resume Tips Integration</a> <a href="#resume-tips-integration" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resume Tips Integration">#</a> </h2> <p>The tool ships with a companion reference at <code>RESUME_TIPS.md</code> (also in the GitHub repo) that covers:</p> <ul> <li>How ATS systems actually score resumes</li> <li>Formatting rules that matter and what breaks parsers</li> <li>Writing summaries, bullets, and skills sections that work</li> <li>Keyword strategy without stuffing</li> <li>Cover letter tone and structure</li> <li>Pre-submission checklist</li> </ul> <p><em>Read it before running the tool to understand what the scores mean.</em></p> <hr> <h2 id="frequently-asked-questions"> <a href="#frequently-asked-questions" title="Frequently Asked Questions">Frequently Asked Questions</a> <a href="#frequently-asked-questions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Frequently Asked Questions">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="does-the-tool-store-my-resume"> <a href="#does-the-tool-store-my-resume" title="Does the tool store my resume?">Does the tool store my resume?</a> <a href="#does-the-tool-store-my-resume" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Does the tool store my resume?">#</a> </h3> <p>No. The app is entirely client-side. Nothing is persisted to any server. Session data lives in browser memory and disappears when you close the tab.</p> <h3 id="my-resume-scored-low--should-i-panic"> <a href="#my-resume-scored-low--should-i-panic" title="My resume scored low — should I panic?">My resume scored low — should I panic?</a> <a href="#my-resume-scored-low--should-i-panic" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="My resume scored low — should I panic?">#</a> </h3> <p>ATS scores are directional, not pass/fail. A score of 60 in the tool does not mean an ATS will reject you — it means there are measurable gaps between your resume and the specific job description you analyzed. Use the score to prioritize edits, not as a verdict.</p> <h3 id="can-i-use-it-with-multiple-job-descriptions"> <a href="#can-i-use-it-with-multiple-job-descriptions" title="Can I use it with multiple job descriptions?">Can I use it with multiple job descriptions?</a> <a href="#can-i-use-it-with-multiple-job-descriptions" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Can I use it with multiple job descriptions?">#</a> </h3> <p>Yes. Paste a new job description at any time. The keyword analysis and optimization will re-run against the new posting. Each analysis is independent.</p> <h3 id="is-the-ollama-integration-really-offline"> <a href="#is-the-ollama-integration-really-offline" title="Is the Ollama integration really offline?">Is the Ollama integration really offline?</a> <a href="#is-the-ollama-integration-really-offline" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Is the Ollama integration really offline?">#</a> </h3> <p>Yes, if Ollama is running on your local machine or on a machine on your local network. The app sends text to your Ollama instance over HTTP — nothing goes to any external service.</p> <h3 id="how-accurate-is-the-resume-type-detection"> <a href="#how-accurate-is-the-resume-type-detection" title="How accurate is the resume type detection?">How accurate is the resume type detection?</a> <a href="#how-accurate-is-the-resume-type-detection" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="How accurate is the resume type detection?">#</a> </h3> <p>The detector runs a rule-based heuristic on your resume content — looking at years of experience mentioned, presence of education indicators, publication or research sections, and career gap signals. It works well for most resumes but can be wrong for unusual career profiles. The section ordering it applies is always adjustable.</p> <hr> <h2 id="project-roadmap"> <a href="#project-roadmap" title="Project Roadmap">Project Roadmap</a> <a href="#project-roadmap" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Project Roadmap">#</a> </h2> <p>Features in development or planned:</p> <ul> <li>Resume version history via IndexedDB</li> <li>LinkedIn profile optimizer</li> <li>Google Gemini provider support</li> <li>Additional Ollama models</li> </ul> <p>The project is MIT licensed and welcomes pull requests. Open an issue first for major changes.</p> <hr> <h2 id="conclusion"> <a href="#conclusion" title="Conclusion">Conclusion</a> <a href="#conclusion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Conclusion">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>ATS Resume Improver</strong> fills a real gap: a tool that does serious resume analysis without brokering your data to anyone. The no-key mode gives you instant, actionable feedback on formatting and keyword coverage. Adding an AI key upgrades the analysis to semantic reasoning, cover letter writing, and interview prep — all for pennies per analysis or completely free with Ollama.</p> <p>The live hosted version is at <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="atsresumeimprover.netlify.app"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/"> <a href="https://atsresumeimprover.netlify.app/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >atsresumeimprover.netlify.app</a> </span> </strong>. The full source is at <strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver"> <a href="https://github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >github.com/simeononsecurity/ats-resume-improver</a> </span> </strong>.</p> <p>If you’re self-hosting for your own job search or want to customize the scoring weights and prompts for a specific industry, the Docker setup and clean project structure make it straightforward to fork and adapt.</p> <hr> <h2 id="resume-optimization-course"> <a href="#resume-optimization-course" title="Resume Optimization Course">Resume Optimization Course</a> <a href="#resume-optimization-course" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Resume Optimization Course">#</a> </h2> <p>If you want a structured, step-by-step guide for applying everything this tool scores, read the companion course:</p> <p><strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Resume Optimization Course: Beat ATS Systems and Land More Interviews"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/resume-optimization-course-start/"> <a href="/resume-optimization-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Resume Optimization Course: Beat ATS Systems and Land More Interviews</a> </span> </strong> — 9 modules covering ATS scoring, formatting, bullet points, keywords, tailoring, cover letters, and the pre-send checklist. Use the tool alongside the course for immediate feedback at each step.</p> <hr> <h2 id="references"> <a href="#references" title="References">References</a> <a href="#references" class="h-anchor" item.title: AWS and Cloud Developer Certifications: The Complete Guide
item.category: "AWS developer certification" , "AWS Solutions Architect" , "Azure developer certification" , "Google Cloud developer certification" , "cloud certifications for developers" , "AWS DVA-C02" , "AZ-204" , "cloud certification guide 2026"
item.description: A complete guide to AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud certifications for software developers — which ones to get, in what order, and what each one proves to employers.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook"> <a href="#click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook" title=" Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook-start/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook-start/" rel="follow me" >Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook</a> </span> </a> <a href="#click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>Cloud certifications are the category of credentials that provide the most concrete career benefit for software developers.</strong> Cloud is now the default deployment environment for virtually all production software. A developer who can write application code AND understand AWS Lambda, API Gateway, RDS, S3, and IAM is materially more valuable than one who cannot. <em>Earning a cloud certification before your job search is one of the highest-ROI investments early-career developers can make.</em></p> <h2 id="which-cloud-provider-to-certify-in"> <a href="#which-cloud-provider-to-certify-in" title="Which Cloud Provider to Certify In">Which Cloud Provider to Certify In</a> <a href="#which-cloud-provider-to-certify-in" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Which Cloud Provider to Certify In">#</a> </h2> <p>Choose based on your target job market and the companies you want to work for.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Provider</th> <th>Market Share</th> <th>Best For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>AWS (Amazon)</strong></td> <td>~31% globally (largest)</td> <td>Widely applicable; most recognized by employers</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Azure (Microsoft)</strong></td> <td>~25% globally</td> <td>Enterprise environments, Microsoft shops, government/DoD</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Google Cloud (GCP)</strong></td> <td>~11% globally</td> <td>Data-heavy companies, ML/AI workloads, Google-aligned orgs</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><em>AWS certifications have the broadest employer recognition. Start with AWS unless your target company explicitly uses Azure or GCP.</em></p> <h2 id="aws-certification-path-for-developers"> <a href="#aws-certification-path-for-developers" title="AWS Certification Path for Developers">AWS Certification Path for Developers</a> <a href="#aws-certification-path-for-developers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="AWS Certification Path for Developers">#</a> </h2> <p>AWS organizes certifications into three tiers: Foundational, Associate, and Professional.</p> <h3 id="tier-1-foundational"> <a href="#tier-1-foundational" title="Tier 1: Foundational">Tier 1: Foundational</a> <a href="#tier-1-foundational" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Tier 1: Foundational">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: cloud concepts, AWS global infrastructure, core services overview, billing and pricing.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers with zero AWS exposure; a prerequisite for Associate-level depth.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 2 to 4 weeks.</li> <li><strong>Exam format</strong>: 65 multiple choice and multiple response questions; 90 minutes; passing score ~700/1000.</li> </ul> <h3 id="tier-2-associate"> <a href="#tier-2-associate" title="Tier 2: Associate">Tier 2: Associate</a> <a href="#tier-2-associate" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Tier 2: Associate">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>AWS Certified Developer – Associate (DVA-C02)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: developing, deploying, and debugging cloud-native applications on AWS. Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3, CodePipeline, CloudFormation, IAM for developers.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers actively building applications on AWS.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 6 to 8 weeks with hands-on practice.</li> <li><strong>Why it matters</strong>: directly relevant to your day-to-day work as a backend or full stack developer in AWS environments.</li> </ul> <p><strong>AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: designing distributed systems, selecting appropriate AWS services, cost optimization, security architecture.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers moving toward cloud engineering, architecture, or DevOps.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 8 to 12 weeks.</li> <li><strong>Why it matters</strong>: the most widely held and recognized AWS certification; opens roles in cloud engineering and architecture.</li> </ul> <h3 id="tier-3-professional"> <a href="#tier-3-professional" title="Tier 3: Professional">Tier 3: Professional</a> <a href="#tier-3-professional" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Tier 3: Professional">#</a> </h3> <p><strong>AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional (SAP-C02)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: advanced architecture for complex, large-scale deployments; migration strategies; cost optimization at scale.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: experienced cloud engineers or senior developers with 2+ years of hands-on AWS.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 10 to 16 weeks.</li> </ul> <p><em>Earn Associate before attempting Professional. Professional without real AWS experience is very difficult to pass.</em></p> <h2 id="azure-certification-path-for-developers"> <a href="#azure-certification-path-for-developers" title="Azure Certification Path for Developers">Azure Certification Path for Developers</a> <a href="#azure-certification-path-for-developers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Azure Certification Path for Developers">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Microsoft Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: developing solutions with Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Azure Storage, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Active Directory, Azure API Management, and Azure DevOps.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers building applications in Azure environments.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 6 to 8 weeks.</li> <li><strong>Why it matters</strong>: required or heavily preferred for developer roles at enterprise companies running on Azure.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305)</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: designing Azure-based solutions covering identity, governance, data, business continuity, and infrastructure.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: senior developers and cloud architects.</li> <li><strong>Prerequisite</strong>: AZ-104 (Azure Administrator) or equivalent experience recommended.</li> </ul> <h2 id="google-cloud-certification-path-for-developers"> <a href="#google-cloud-certification-path-for-developers" title="Google Cloud Certification Path for Developers">Google Cloud Certification Path for Developers</a> <a href="#google-cloud-certification-path-for-developers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Google Cloud Certification Path for Developers">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Google Associate Cloud Engineer</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: deploying applications, monitoring operations, and managing GCP infrastructure including Compute Engine, Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, and Cloud Operations.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers working in GCP environments.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 6 to 8 weeks.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Google Professional Cloud Developer</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>What it covers</strong>: building scalable applications, designing APIs, implementing CI/CD pipelines, and managing cloud resources programmatically.</li> <li><strong>Who it is for</strong>: developers building production applications on GCP.</li> <li><strong>Study time</strong>: 10 to 14 weeks of study plus real project experience.</li> </ul> <h2 id="preparation-resources"> <a href="#preparation-resources" title="Preparation Resources">Preparation Resources</a> <a href="#preparation-resources" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Preparation Resources">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Resource</th> <th>For</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>AWS Skill Builder</strong> (free)</td> <td>AWS exam prep labs and courses</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stephane Maarek (Udemy)</strong></td> <td>Best-rated AWS Developer and Solutions Architect courses</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>A Cloud Guru / Pluralsight</strong></td> <td>All three cloud providers; hands-on labs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TutorialsDojo</strong></td> <td>Practice exams with detailed explanations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Microsoft Learn</strong> (free)</td> <td>Azure certification study paths</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Google Cloud Skills Boost</strong> (free)</td> <td>GCP learning paths and Qwiklabs</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Developer Certifications Worth Getting"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook/education-and-certifications/developer-certifications-worth-getting/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook/education-and-certifications/developer-certifications-worth-getting/" rel="follow me" >Developer Certifications Worth Getting</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Development Specializations"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-started-in-software-development/software-development-specializations/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-started-in-software-development/software-development-specializations/" rel="follow me" >Software Development Specializations</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Development Career Playbook Home"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook-start/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook-start/" rel="follow me" >Software Development Career Playbook Home</a> </span> </li> </ul> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.ch/

The scarcity is not content — it is structure and follow-through. <em>Pick one primary resource, commit to completing it, and build something with what you learn before moving to the next resource.</em></p> <h2 id="free-structured-courses"> <a href="#free-structured-courses" title="Free Structured Courses">Free Structured Courses</a> <a href="#free-structured-courses" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Free Structured Courses">#</a> </h2> <p>These are the best free, structured learning paths for absolute beginners and career changers.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Resource</th> <th>Best For</th> <th>Why It Works</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="freeCodeCamp"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.freecodecamp.org/"> <a href="https://www.freecodecamp.org/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >freeCodeCamp</a> </span> </strong></td> <td>Web development, JavaScript</td> <td>Project-based curriculum, certifications, huge community</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="The Odin Project"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.theodinproject.com/"> <a href="https://www.theodinproject.com/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >The Odin Project</a> </span> </strong></td> <td>Full stack web development</td> <td>Open source, projects-first, covers HTML through Node.js</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong> <span itemscope item.title: Building a Developer Portfolio in 2026
item.category: "developer portfolio 2026" , "developer portfolio AI era" , "software developer portfolio AI" , "GitHub portfolio 2026" , "portfolio projects AI" , "developer proof of work" , "building developer portfolio" , "portfolio vs certifications 2026"
item.description: In 2026, your developer portfolio is your career. AI can generate resumes and even code, but it cannot fake a well-documented, continuously evolved GitHub portfolio with real commit history and architectural decision records.
item.content:encoded: <h4 id="click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook"> <a href="#click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook" title=" Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook "> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook-start/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook-start/" rel="follow me" >Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook</a> </span> </a> <a href="#click-here-to-return-to-the-software-development-career-playbook" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title=" Click Here to Return To the Software Development Career Playbook ">#</a> </h4> <p><strong>In 2026, your portfolio is the only thing that distinguishes you from every other developer who used AI to write their resume and pass their take-home assessment.</strong> A portfolio of real, documented, deployed, and continuously maintained projects is proof of work — the kind that hiring managers actively look for because they have seen what happens when they do not. <em>Three real projects with genuine documentation and an ability to defend every architectural decision are worth more than a dozen tutorial clones and a stack of certificates.</em></p> <h2 id="why-portfolio-matters-more-than-ever-in-2026"> <a href="#why-portfolio-matters-more-than-ever-in-2026" title="Why Portfolio Matters More Than Ever in 2026">Why Portfolio Matters More Than Ever in 2026</a> <a href="#why-portfolio-matters-more-than-ever-in-2026" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Why Portfolio Matters More Than Ever in 2026">#</a> </h2> <p>Generative AI has changed what “qualified” looks like from the outside:</p> <ul> <li>Anyone can get an AI to generate a professional-sounding resume.</li> <li>Anyone can get an AI to complete a take-home coding project with clean, well-commented code.</li> <li>Anyone can use AI-assisted study tools to pass a certification exam without deeply understanding the material.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Hiring managers at competent engineering teams know this.</strong> The response has been to probe harder in interviews, review GitHub contribution history and commit content, and specifically look for evidence of independent judgment — decisions the candidate cannot explain unless they made them themselves.</p> <p>Your portfolio’s job is to create that evidence before the interview starts.</p> <h2 id="what-a-strong-portfolio-proves-in-2026"> <a href="#what-a-strong-portfolio-proves-in-2026" title="What a Strong Portfolio Proves in 2026">What a Strong Portfolio Proves in 2026</a> <a href="#what-a-strong-portfolio-proves-in-2026" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What a Strong Portfolio Proves in 2026">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>What You Show</th> <th>What It Proves</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Real commit history on a project over months</strong></td> <td>You actually worked on this over time. AI cannot fake six months of evolving commits.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Architectural decision records (ADRs)</strong></td> <td>You understood why you made technical choices, not just that you made them</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>An incident log or postmortem on a production bug</strong></td> <td>You ran something under real conditions, it broke, and you fixed it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Multiple iterations of the same component</strong></td> <td>You learned from feedback and improved. Growth is visible in the code.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Open source PR that was merged</strong></td> <td>An experienced maintainer reviewed your work and accepted it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>A deployed app with real users or traffic</strong></td> <td>You shipped something that exists outside your local environment</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="the-three-project-baseline-2026-version"> <a href="#the-three-project-baseline-2026-version" title="The Three-Project Baseline (2026 Version)">The Three-Project Baseline (2026 Version)</a> <a href="#the-three-project-baseline-2026-version" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The Three-Project Baseline (2026 Version)">#</a> </h2> <p>The bar has risen since 2022. “Built a to-do app” is table stakes. “Built a to-do app and deployed it on AWS with Terraform and a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline, monitored with Grafana, and here are the three bugs I found in production and the commits that fixed them” is a portfolio entry.</p> <p>Every developer needs at minimum three projects at this standard:</p> <p><strong>Project 1: A full-stack application you deployed and maintained</strong></p> <ul> <li>Not just built. Deployed. Running somewhere real (Vercel, Render, Railway, Fly.io, AWS, VPS).</li> <li>Has a CHANGELOG or commit history showing it evolved over time.</li> <li>Has at least one documented bug fix or feature addition made after the initial build.</li> <li>README explains what it does, why you built it, what you learned, and how to run it.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Project 2: An infrastructure or automation project</strong></p> <ul> <li>A Terraform repo that provisions something (even on free tier).</li> <li>A CI/CD pipeline for a real application.</li> <li>An Ansible playbook that configures a server or set of servers.</li> <li>A self-hosted application stack with Docker Compose and documented monitoring.</li> </ul> <p>This signals you understand the full software lifecycle past the “write code” step. Most bootcamp graduates and many CS graduates cannot show this.</p> <p><strong>Project 3: Something that required you to solve a real problem</strong></p> <ul> <li>An automation tool that solved something annoying in your own life.</li> <li>A data pipeline that processes real data you cared about.</li> <li>A contribution to an open source project you actually use.</li> <li>A homelab component with documented architecture and incident history.</li> </ul> <p>The “real problem” project is the interview conversation starter. “I built a thing that monitors my homelab services and pages me when they go down, because my Proxmox cluster was having random DNS failures and I needed immediate visibility” is a story. “I built a weather app” is not.</p> <h2 id="github-profile-standards-in-2026"> <a href="#github-profile-standards-in-2026" title="GitHub Profile Standards in 2026">GitHub Profile Standards in 2026</a> <a href="#github-profile-standards-in-2026" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="GitHub Profile Standards in 2026">#</a> </h2> <p>Your GitHub profile is the first thing most hiring managers check after your resume. The standard is higher than it was two years ago.</p> <p><strong>Profile elements that matter:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Profile README</strong>: a brief, professional introduction with your focus area, skills, and links to your top projects. Link to a personal site or portfolio page if you have one.</li> <li><strong>Pinned repositories</strong>: pin your three to five best projects. Every pinned repo needs a description.</li> <li><strong>Contribution graph</strong>: consistent activity matters. A profile that is completely dead for six months raises questions. You do not need to commit every day, but you should be building something regularly.</li> <li><strong>Repository quality</strong>: every repository should have a clear name, a description, a README, and appropriate topics/tags.</li> <li><strong>Commit message quality</strong>: <code>fix bug</code> or <code>stuff</code> as commit messages signals careless habits. Meaningful commit messages are a professional signal.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What interviewers look for beyond the surface:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Do the commits show evolving understanding or a one-time dump?</li> <li>Do the README files explain context or just list installation steps?</li> <li>Are there any signs of real-world usage (stars, forks, issues from others, CI passing badges)?</li> <li>Is there anything that could not have been written by AI in one sitting?</li> </ul> <h2 id="documentation-that-differentiates-you"> <a href="#documentation-that-differentiates-you" title="Documentation That Differentiates You">Documentation That Differentiates You</a> <a href="#documentation-that-differentiates-you" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Documentation That Differentiates You">#</a> </h2> <p>The documentation in and around your projects is where you create the proof that you understood what you built. The minimum documentation per project:</p> <ol> <li><strong>README</strong> — what it is, why you built it, the tech stack, how to run it locally, and notable implementation decisions.</li> <li><strong>Architecture decision records</strong> — for any non-obvious technical choices, one paragraph explaining why you chose X over Y. “I chose PostgreSQL because the data is relational and transaction integrity matters for this use case” is sufficient.</li> <li><strong>CHANGELOG or notable commits</strong> — what changed over time and why.</li> <li><strong>Incident or debug log</strong> — if anything broke and you fixed it, document it. Even a paragraph: “Discovered that the session middleware was not persisting correctly in production due to a secure cookie setting. Fixed by adding trust proxy configuration.”</li> </ol> <p>This documentation is what you reference in interviews. “The incident I found most interesting in this project was…” is a conversation that only works if you ran something real long enough to hit real problems.</p> <h2 id="homelab-as-portfolio-component"> <a href="#homelab-as-portfolio-component" title="Homelab as Portfolio Component">Homelab as Portfolio Component</a> <a href="#homelab-as-portfolio-component" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Homelab as Portfolio Component">#</a> </h2> <p>For backend, DevOps, platform, or security developers, a well-documented homelab is a portfolio component as powerful as any deployed project. See the parallel guidance in the IT Career Playbook: <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Building an IT Home Lab"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/it-career-playbook/getting-started-in-it/building-an-it-home-lab/"> <a href="/it-career-playbook/getting-started-in-it/building-an-it-home-lab/" rel="follow me" >Building an IT Home Lab</a> </span> .</p> <p>A self-hosted development environment with:</p> <ul> <li>Multiple services running under Docker Compose or Kubernetes</li> <li>Infrastructure-as-code managing the configuration</li> <li>Monitoring and alerting configured</li> <li>Git-tracked configuration and runbooks</li> <li>An incident log showing real problems diagnosed and resolved</li> </ul> <p>…is direct evidence of production-adjacent skill that most junior candidates cannot show.</p> <h2 id="what-not-to-do"> <a href="#what-not-to-do" title="What Not To Do">What Not To Do</a> <a href="#what-not-to-do" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What Not To Do">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Do not list projects you cannot explain at depth.</strong> If an interviewer asks “why did you choose this approach?” and you do not have a real answer, you have lost credibility.</li> <li><strong>Do not pad with tutorial projects.</strong> Every hiring manager has seen the “I followed a YouTube tutorial for this” project. Flag your learning projects honestly or leave them off.</li> <li><strong>Do not have a GitHub with no activity for six months and call it a portfolio.</strong> A static portfolio looks like someone who stopped learning.</li> <li><strong>Do not use AI to write your portfolio project READMEs without reviewing them.</strong> AI-generated READMEs often have a recognizable pattern and feel generic. Write your own descriptions in your own voice.</li> </ul> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Is Software Development a Good Career?"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-started-in-software-development/is-software-development-a-good-career/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-started-in-software-development/is-software-development-a-good-career/" rel="follow me" >Is Software Development a Good Career?</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Developer Resume Writing Tips"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-a-job-as-a-developer/software-developer-resume-writing-tips/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook/getting-a-job-as-a-developer/software-developer-resume-writing-tips/" rel="follow me" >Software Developer Resume Writing Tips</a> </span> </li> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Development Career Playbook Home"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/software-development-career-playbook-start/"> <a href="/software-development-career-playbook-start/" rel="follow me" >Software Development Career Playbook Home</a> </span> </li> </ul> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.ch/
